problem: Given that $r=\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta -2$ for $\theta =\theta (t),$ and that $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=-3$ at the point where $\theta =\pi ,$ find $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$

feedback.worked_solution:
Differentiating the given relation with respect to $t$ using implicit differentiation, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =5\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta  \\ \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(r) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}\theta }(5\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (5\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta ).\end{aligned}
$$

Now we can substitute the given information $\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}=-3$ and $\theta =\frac{\pi }{6},$ and solve for $\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t}.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}\theta }{\text{d}t}\cdot (5\operatorname{sec}⁡\theta \operatorname{tan}⁡\theta ) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =(-3)\cdot (5\operatorname{sec}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =(-3)\cdot 5\cdot (\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\cdot \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}) \\ \frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} & =-10.\end{aligned}
$$
